skills.description: Design a detailed value proposition using a 6-part JTBD template — Who, Why, What before, How, What after, Alternatives. Use when creating a value proposition, analyzing customer value delivery, or articulating why customers should choose your product.

skills.name: draft-nda
skills.description: Draft a detailed Non-Disclosure Agreement between two parties covering information types, jurisdiction, and clauses needing legal review. Use when creating confidentiality agreements or preparing an NDA for a partnership.

skills.name: grammar-check
skills.description: Identify grammar, logical, and flow errors in text and suggest targeted fixes without rewriting the entire text. Use when proofreading content, checking writing quality, or reviewing a draft.

skills.name: privacy-policy
skills.description: Draft a detailed privacy policy covering data types, jurisdiction, GDPR and compliance considerations, and clauses needing legal review. Use when creating a privacy policy, updating data protection documentation, or preparing for compliance.

skills.name: review-resume
skills.description: Comprehensive PM resume review and tailoring against 10 best practices including XYZ+S formula, keyword optimization, job-specific tailoring, and structure. Use when reviewing a PM resume, preparing for job applications, or improving resume impact.

skills.name: ab-testing
skills.description: When the user wants to plan, run, or read A/B tests, or asks a judgement call on one: is the result real, can we stop, which version won, is this worth testing at all: sample size, duration, significance, hypotheses, and experiment backlogs. For tracking setup, see analytics. For page-level conversion fixes, see cro.

skills.name: ad-creative
skills.description: When the user wants to write or judge ad creative, or asks which ad, hook, or angle to run or kill: headlines, primary text, and variations for Google, Meta, LinkedIn, and TikTok, fresh angles when creative fatigues. Test hypotheses name the metric, comparison, and expected direction. No AI tells like 'it's not X, it's Y'. For campaign strategy, see ads. For landing pages, see copywriting.

skills.name: ads
skills.description: When the user wants to plan, run, or fix paid ads on Google, Meta, and LinkedIn, or asks a judgement call on them: are ads worth it, which channel or budget split, why CPA rose, kill or keep a campaign. End with facts, hypotheses, and missing data; label unavailable inputs MISSING instead of estimating. For ad copy, see ad-creative. For pixels and CAPI, see conversion-tracking. For landing pages, see cro.

skills.name: ai-seo
skills.description: When the user wants to get cited and recommended in AI answers (ChatGPT, Perplexity, AI Overviews), or asks why AI cites a competitor, which content gets cited, or whether llms.txt or a page format is worth it: AEO, GEO, AI visibility, agent-readable sites. For technical and on-page SEO, see seo-audit. For structured data, see schema.

skills.name: analytics
skills.description: When the user wants to set up or audit analytics, or asks whether a metric or number is calculated right, what to track, or how to name events: tracking plans, GA4, GTM, Mixpanel, PostHog, UTMs. Rate metrics divide matching closed windows, never full-period spend by partial-period results. For conversions in ad platforms, see conversion-tracking. For attribution or platforms that over-claim, see attribution. For tests, see ab-testing.

skills.name: aso
skills.description: When the user wants to audit or optimize an App Store or Google Play listing, or asks which title, keywords, or screenshots to pick or why downloads are low: subtitle, description, ratings, and comparing listings with competitors.

skills.name: attribution
skills.description: When the user wants to work out which marketing drives revenue, or asks whether a channel is really working, which numbers to trust, or how to credit podcasts and dark social: attribution models, platforms that over-claim, MMM, incrementality and holdout tests, self-reported attribution. For tracking and UTMs, see analytics. For pixels and CAPI, see conversion-tracking. For CRM revenue, see revops. For AI search blind spots, see ai-seo.

skills.name: churn-prevention
skills.description: When the user wants to reduce churn, or asks why customers cancel, whether to offer a discount or pause: cancellation flows, exit surveys, save offers, dunning and failed-payment recovery. For win-back emails, see emails. For in-app upgrade screens, see paywalls.

skills.name: co-marketing
skills.description: When the user wants co-marketing partners or joint campaigns, or asks whether a partner fits, a size mismatch matters, or how to split work and leads: integration partners, cross-promotion, co-branded content, joint webinars. For referral programs, see referrals. For launch partnerships, see launch. For running the event, see events.

skills.name: cold-email
skills.description: When the user wants to write or run B2B cold outbound, or asks whether an opener, reason to reach out, or email works or why nobody replies: cold emails, follow-ups, sending domains, deliverability, LinkedIn, cadences. Send from secondary domains, verify lists first, turn off open tracking, stop every channel when a prospect replies. No AI tells like 'it's not X, it's Y'. For the list, see prospecting. For lifecycle email, see emails. For call scripts, see sales-enablement.

skills.name: community-marketing
skills.description: When the user wants to build or grow an online community, or asks whether a community is worth it, where to host it, or why members stay quiet: Discord, Slack, forums, participation, community-led growth, advocates. For referral programs, see referrals. For creator partnerships, see influencer-marketing.

skills.name: competitor-profiling
skills.description: When the user wants to research competitors into dated profiles, or asks what a rival charges, claims, or is doing, or whether a conclusion about them is fair: positioning, pricing, features, reviews, SEO, observed facts kept apart from inference. For comparison pages, see competitors. For battle cards, see sales-enablement. For accounts you sell to, see prospecting. For how a competitor grew, see reverse-engineer-marketing.

skills.name: competitors
skills.description: When the user wants to create or audit comparison and alternative pages ('X vs Y', 'X alternative', 'best X alternatives'), or asks what a public page may say about a competitor: page formats, fair claims, and outdated pages. For researching competitors, see competitor-profiling. For internal battle cards, see sales-enablement.

skills.name: content-strategy
skills.description: When the user wants to plan content, or asks which topic or piece to prioritize, what to write about, or why posts bring no customers: topic clusters, editorial calendars, roadmaps tied to customers and search. For writing pieces, see copywriting. For SEO audits, see seo-audit. For social content, see social.

skills.name: conversion-tracking
skills.description: When the user wants to set up, audit, or fix conversion tracking to Google Ads, Meta, GA4, LinkedIn, and TikTok, or asks why conversions are missing or doubled: GTM, pixels, CAPI, Enhanced Conversions, offline imports. Fire on confirmed success, not the submit click; verify a test conversion arrives; diagnose before changing; offer free paths and disclose partner tools. For tracking plans, see analytics. For attribution, see attribution. For bidding, see ads.

skills.name: copy-editing
skills.description: When the user wants to edit, tighten, proofread, or refresh existing copy, or asks whether to keep, cut, or change a line in it, without rewriting from scratch. Every edit removes AI tells: 'it's not X, it's Y' reveals, 'no X, no Y, no Z' lists, and sentences that trail into extra comma clauses. A request to fix one line gets a point edit to that line only. For new copy, see copywriting.

skills.name: copywriting
skills.description: When the user wants to write or rewrite page copy (homepage, landing, pricing, feature), or asks which headline, promise, or message to lead with. Diagnoses the input first (blank brief, real voice, or point edit) and changes only what it calls for. Claims must be supportable; a declined claim names the evidence that would unlock it. No AI tells like 'it's not X, it's Y' or 'no X, no Y, no Z'. For editing, see copy-editing. For emails, see emails. For the offer, see offers.

skills.name: cro
skills.description: When the user wants more conversions from a page or form, or asks why a page isn't converting, what to change first, or whether to add or remove a field or element: landing and pricing pages, lead forms, or a URL shared for feedback. For signup flows, see signup. For activation, see onboarding. For popups, see popups. For running the test, see ab-testing.

skills.name: customer-research
skills.description: When the user wants to run or synthesize customer research, or asks what customer quotes, reviews, or feedback really mean, what is safe to conclude, and what to ask next: interviews, surveys, voice of customer, personas, JTBD, mining Reddit and reviews. For copy from research, see copywriting. For acting on it in pages, see cro.

skills.name: directory-submissions
skills.description: When the user wants to list a product in startup, SaaS, AI, MCP, and review directories, or asks which directories are worth it or whether listings are working: Product Hunt, G2, Capterra, AlternativeTo, MCP registries, awesome lists, and a submission tracker. For the broader launch, see launch. For other link building, see link-building.

skills.name: emails
skills.description: When the user wants to create or improve automated email sequences, or asks what to send, when, or whether an email or flow is working: welcome, onboarding, nurture, and win-back flows. No AI tells like 'it's not X, it's Y', 'no X, no Y, no Z' lists, or fake 'Re:' subject lines. For cold outreach, see cold-email. For in-app onboarding, see onboarding. For texts, see sms.

skills.name: events
skills.description: When the user wants to plan, run, sponsor, or speak at events, or asks whether an event or booth is worth the money: webinars, conferences, booths, meetups, show-up rates, and follow-up into pipeline. For launches, see launch. For joint webinars, see co-marketing. For community programs, see community-marketing. For podcasts, see public-relations. For event emails, see emails.

skills.name: free-tools
skills.description: When the user wants to plan or build a free tool as marketing, or asks whether a tool idea is worth building or which one to pick: calculators, graders, generators, and other interactive tools for leads, SEO, and links. For downloadable lead magnets, see lead-magnets.

skills.name: image
skills.description: When the user wants to create, generate, edit, or optimize marketing images, or asks which approach to take (generate, design, or photograph): blog heroes, social graphics, product mockups, banners, OG images. For ad images, see ad-creative. For video, see video.

skills.name: influencer-marketing
skills.description: When the user wants creator, influencer, or ambassador partnerships, or asks which creators fit, what to pay, which rights to buy, or whether a sponsorship worked: vetting, contracts, briefs, UGC, newsletter and podcast sponsorships, FTC disclosure. For affiliate payouts, see referrals. For community advocacy, see community-marketing. For creator content as ads, see ad-creative.

skills.name: launch
skills.description: When the user wants to plan a product or feature launch, or asks whether it's ready, when to announce, or how to get noticed: Product Hunt, beta and early access, waitlists, release go-to-market, launch checklists, release notes. For marketing after launch, see marketing-ideas. For the offer, see offers.

skills.name: lead-magnets
skills.description: When the user wants to plan or improve a lead magnet, or asks what to give away for emails or how much to ask in return (gating, form fields): checklists, templates, ebooks, gated guides, content upgrades. For interactive tools, see free-tools. For the follow-up sequence, see emails. For popups that capture emails, see popups.

skills.name: link-building
skills.description: When the user wants backlinks and mentions that lift rankings and AI citations, or asks how to get sites to link or whether a link tactic is safe: link gaps, unlinked mentions, broken links, guest posts, best-of outreach. Never buy links that pass ranking credit: paid or exchanged placements get rel=sponsored or nofollow. For press, see public-relations. For directories, see directory-submissions. For reviews, see referrals. For communities, see community-marketing.

skills.name: marketing-council
skills.description: When the user wants several expert takes on a marketing decision, or asks what a famous marketer would say about it: a simulated board (Seth Godin, David Ogilvy, April Dunford, Byron Sharp, and more), each grounded in their documented frameworks, where they disagree, and a recommendation. To execute, hand off to the relevant skill.

skills.name: marketing-ideas
skills.description: When the user wants marketing ideas or growth tactics for a software product, or asks what to try to get attention or the next customers with little time or budget, or after the obvious channels. Draws on a library of 139 ideas. For a specific channel, see that skill (ads, social, emails, and others). For a full plan, see marketing-plan.

skills.name: marketing-loops
skills.description: When the user wants a recurring marketing job an AI agent runs on a cadence or trigger, or asks what a weekly or daily automated check should do, remember, and when it should stop: SEO and ads checks, churn watches, outbound triage. For one-off ideas, see marketing-ideas. For the test loop, see ab-testing.

skills.name: marketing-plan
skills.description: When the user wants a full marketing or go-to-market plan for a client, an advised company, or their own product, or asks how to sequence or prioritize several initiatives with a fixed team and budget: channels, budget, team, goals across AARRR, market sizing. For positioning first, see product-marketing. For ideas only, see marketing-ideas.

skills.name: marketing-psychology
skills.description: When the user wants to apply psychology to marketing, or asks why buyers behave or value things as they do, or whether a persuasion tactic is honest: biases, mental models, anchoring, social proof, scarcity, loss aversion, framing. For a page, see cro. For pricing tactics, see pricing. For copy, see copywriting.

skills.name: offers
skills.description: When the user wants to design or improve the offer itself, or asks why it isn't selling or how to add urgency honestly: value stacking, bonuses, guarantees, scarcity, payment plans, upsells. Best for services, courses, coaching, and high-ticket B2B; for self-serve SaaS, read pricing first. For price and tiers, see pricing. For the page, see copywriting. For the launch, see launch. For sales collateral, see sales-enablement.

skills.name: onboarding
skills.description: When the user wants better onboarding and activation, or asks why new users don't stick or what the first session should do: first-run experience, aha moments, checklists, empty states, time to value. For the signup flow itself, see signup. For onboarding emails, see emails.

skills.name: paywalls
skills.description: When the user wants to create or improve in-app paywalls and upgrade moments, or asks when or how hard to ask free users to pay (after they've seen value): upgrade screens, upsell modals, feature gates, limit-reached and trial-expired screens, mobile subscription paywalls. For public pricing pages, see cro. For pricing decisions, see pricing.

skills.name: popups
skills.description: When the user wants to create or improve popups, modals, slide-ins, sticky bars, and banners, or asks whether one will help or annoy and when to show it: exit intent, email capture, scroll and time triggers, announcements. For forms and pages outside popups, see cro.

skills.name: pricing
skills.description: When the user wants to set pricing and packaging, or asks what to charge, whether to raise prices, or how to move existing customers: tiers, value metrics, per-seat vs usage, freemium and trials, willingness to pay, pricing pages. For in-app upgrade screens, see paywalls. For offers on services, courses, and high-ticket B2B, see offers.

skills.name: product-marketing
skills.description: When the user wants to create or update the product marketing context doc (.agents/product-marketing.md), or asks what belongs in it or whether positioning or ICP is clear enough: product, ICP, positioning, competitors, customer language, brand voice. Use it before other marketing skills on a new project, when the audience or positioning changes, and to log learnings.

skills.name: programmatic-seo
skills.description: When the user wants SEO pages at scale from templates and data, or asks whether a page set will rank or look thin: location, integration, comparison, directory, and '[X] for [Y]' pages, each useful rather than thin. For SEO audits, see seo-audit. For content planning, see content-strategy.

skills.name: prospecting
skills.description: When the user wants to find and qualify prospects for outbound, or asks who to target first, which signal to prioritize, or where to spot buyers with the problem: buying signals, enrichment, verification, account research. Verify emails before a sequence, never scrape LinkedIn: define audiences in Sales Navigator and pull contacts from licensed data. For outreach, see cold-email. For competitor research, see competitor-profiling.

skills.name: public-relations
skills.description: When the user wants press and media coverage, or asks what to say to a reporter, whether a story is newsworthy, or how to handle a crisis: pitches, press releases, media lists, HARO, op-eds, podcast guest prep, newsjacking (public relations, not pull requests). For directories, see directory-submissions. For launches, see launch. For cold outreach to prospects, see cold-email.

skills.name: referrals
skills.description: When the user wants referral and affiliate programs or word of mouth, or asks what to reward, how much to pay, or which loop to start with: refer-a-friend incentives, commissions and payouts, partner programs, 'made with' badges, review campaigns. For launch virality, see launch. For creator deals, see influencer-marketing.

skills.name: reverse-engineer-marketing
skills.description: When the user wants to know how another company grew and what to copy, or asks what a competitor did and when: a dated log of their moves against their traffic from public data, archives, job posts, reviews, and their funnel, compared with the user's data, ending in plays routed to other skills. Also finds where competitors are weak. For a snapshot profile, see competitor-profiling. For comparison pages, see competitors.

skills.name: revops
skills.description: When the user wants to design revenue operations, or asks when a lead is ready for sales or why sales and marketing disagree on lead quality: lifecycle stages, MQL and SQL, scoring, routing, handoff, pipeline stages, CRM automation. For outbound copy, see cold-email. For email flows, see emails.

skills.name: sales-enablement
skills.description: When the user wants sales collateral, or asks what to give a champion or rep, or how to answer an objection or make the case: decks, one-pagers, objection handling, demo scripts, talk tracks, battle cards, proposals, win-loss. For public comparison pages, see competitors. For buyer research, see customer-research. For website copy, see copywriting. For cold emails, see cold-email. For the offer, see offers.

skills.name: schema
skills.description: When the user wants to add, fix, or validate schema markup (JSON-LD), or asks which type fits a page or whether some markup is allowed: product, review, recipe, FAQ, rich result eligibility (FAQ no longer earns Google rich results), Search Console errors. For broader SEO, see seo-audit. For AI search, see ai-seo.

skills.name: seo-audit
skills.description: When the user wants to audit or diagnose SEO, or asks why traffic dropped, a page won't rank, or whether a setup like canonicals, hreflang, or redirects is right: technical SEO, indexing, Google updates, on-page and titles, Core Web Vitals, local SEO. Start here when someone just says their SEO is bad. For pages at scale, see programmatic-seo. For structured data, see schema. For AI search, see ai-seo.

skills.name: signup
skills.description: When the user wants better signup, registration, and trial start flows, or asks which fields or steps to cut or whether to require a card: SSO and drop-off before an account exists. For what happens after signup, see onboarding. For lead forms that don't create an account, see cro.

skills.name: site-architecture
skills.description: When the user wants to plan or restructure a website, or asks which pages they need or where something belongs: hierarchy, navigation, URL structure, internal linking, website builders and migrations. Not XML sitemaps (see seo-audit). For structured data, see schema.

skills.name: sms
skills.description: When the user wants SMS, MMS, or WhatsApp marketing, or asks whether texting is worth it or a message is allowed: abandoned cart, win-back, and promo texts, WhatsApp templates and windows, TCPA and A2P 10DLC compliance, SMS vs email. For email, see emails. For phone capture popups, see popups.

skills.name: social
skills.description: When the user wants organic social content for LinkedIn, X, Instagram, TikTok, or Facebook, or asks what to post, which format to favor, or from which account: posts, threads, carousels, short-form video scripts, calendars, build-in-public posts from commits, listening. No AI tells like 'it's not X, it's Y' or broetry. For content strategy, see content-strategy. For paid ads, see ad-creative. For press, see public-relations.

skills.name: video
skills.description: When the user wants to create video with AI tools or code, or asks which approach to use (screen recording, AI avatar, generated, or templated) or how to make videos repeatably: product demos, AI generation (Veo, Sora, HeyGen), programmatic video with Remotion. For what to post, see social. For video ads, see ad-creative.

skills.name: utility-update-pm-skills
skills.description: Validates internet access, compares the locally installed pm-skills version against the latest public release, and updates local files with conflict-aware overwrite-or-skip options. Produces an update report listing changed files, skipped files, and new capabilities. Use when you want to bring a local pm-skills installation up to date.

skills.name: utility-update-pm-skills
skills.description: Checks for newer pm-skills releases, compares local vs. latest version, previews what would change, and updates local files after user confirmation. Generates a structured update report documenting changed files, new capabilities, and the value delta between versions. Use when you want to bring a local pm-skills installation up to date.

skills.name: define-hypothesis
skills.description: Defines a testable hypothesis with clear success metrics and a validation approach. Use when forming assumptions to test or aligning a team on what success looks like, before any experiment is designed. To design the A/B test or experiment that will validate the hypothesis, use measure-experiment-design.

skills.name: define-jtbd-canvas
skills.description: Creates a Jobs to be Done canvas capturing the functional, emotional, and social dimensions of a customer job. Use when deeply understanding customer motivations, designing for jobs, or reframing product positioning.

skills.name: define-opportunity-tree
skills.description: Creates an opportunity solution tree connecting a desired outcome to customer opportunities and candidate solutions, preventing solution-first jumps in continuous discovery. Use when structuring scattered feature ideas or communicating how the roadmap traces to outcomes. For ranking an existing flat list of candidates, use define-prioritization-framework instead; this skill discovers the list, it does not score one.

skills.name: define-prioritization-framework
skills.description: Run applicable prioritization frameworks (RICE, ICE, MoSCoW, Weighted Scoring, Kano) against a list of features or initiatives. Produces a comparison table showing where rankings agree and diverge across frameworks, and an executive summary with recommendation. Framework applicability is filtered by data availability; Kano requires customer research. Refuses to fabricate scores; produces an estimation scaffold when input data is missing.

skills.name: define-problem-statement
skills.description: Creates a clear problem framing document with user impact, business context, and success criteria. Use when starting a new initiative, realigning a drifted project, or communicating up to leadership.

skills.name: deliver-acceptance-criteria
skills.description: Generates structured Given/When/Then acceptance criteria for a user story or feature slice, covering the happy path, key failure scenarios, and non-functional expectations in testable form. Use when turning requirements into verifiable scenarios for engineering handoff and QA sign-off. For a dedicated catalog of boundary conditions, error states, and recovery paths across a feature, use deliver-edge-cases; to write the stories themselves, use deliver-user-stories.

skills.name: deliver-edge-cases
skills.description: Documents edge cases, error states, boundary conditions, race conditions, and recovery paths for a feature - the systematic catalog of what can go wrong and the failure modes to design for. Use during specification to map the failure surface and ensure comprehensive coverage, or during QA planning to identify boundary and limit scenarios to test. Distinct from deliver-acceptance-criteria, which writes story-level Given/When/Then checks; this skill produces the whole-feature edge-case catalog.

skills.name: deliver-launch-checklist
skills.description: Creates a cross-functional pre-launch checklist covering engineering, design, marketing, support, legal, and operations readiness, with owners, dates, and go/no-go criteria so nothing is missed before release. Use for significant or cross-team launches, not a small single-team change. For the customer-facing announcement of what shipped, use deliver-release-notes instead.

skills.name: deliver-prd
skills.description: Creates a comprehensive Product Requirements Document that aligns stakeholders on what to build, why, and how success will be measured. Use when specifying features, epics, or product initiatives for engineering handoff.

skills.name: deliver-release-notes
skills.description: Creates user-facing release notes that communicate new features, improvements, and fixes in clear, benefit-focused language. Use when shipping updates to communicate changes to users, customers, or stakeholders.

skills.name: deliver-user-stories
skills.description: Generates user stories in the standard persona, action, benefit story format from product requirements or feature descriptions. Use when breaking a feature into stories for sprint planning, writing tickets, or communicating scope to engineering. For testable Given/When/Then acceptance criteria on a story, use deliver-acceptance-criteria; for boundary and failure scenarios, use deliver-edge-cases.

skills.name: develop-adr
skills.description: Creates an Architecture Decision Record following the Nygard format to document significant technical decisions, their context, and consequences. Use when making technical choices that affect system architecture, technology selection, or development patterns.

skills.name: develop-design-rationale
skills.description: Documents the reasoning behind design decisions including alternatives considered, trade-offs evaluated, and principles applied. Use when making significant UX decisions, aligning with stakeholders on design direction, or preserving design context for future reference.

skills.name: develop-solution-brief
skills.description: Creates a concise one-page solution overview that communicates the proposed approach, key decisions, and trade-offs. Use when pitching solutions to stakeholders, aligning teams on approach, or documenting solution intent before detailed specification.

skills.name: develop-spike-summary
skills.description: Documents the results of a completed technical or design spike, capturing the original question, approach, evidence-backed findings, and a clear proceed-or-not recommendation so the team does not re-litigate the exploration. Use once a time-boxed investigation has concluded. For the architecture decision the spike informs, use develop-adr instead; for research-based exploration, use discover-interview-synthesis.

skills.name: discover-competitive-analysis
skills.description: Creates a structured competitive analysis comparing features, pricing, and positioning across 3-5 direct and indirect competitors, with a 2x2 map and actionable strategic recommendations. Use before entering a market, planning differentiation, or after losing deals. For market size rather than competitor positioning, use discover-market-sizing instead.

skills.name: discover-interview-synthesis
skills.description: Synthesizes user research interviews into actionable insights, patterns, and recommendations. Use after conducting user interviews, customer calls, or usability sessions to extract and communicate findings across participants. Distinct from foundation-meeting-recap, which summarizes one internal meeting for its attendees; this skill aggregates research conversations into evidence-backed findings.

skills.name: discover-journey-map
skills.description: Maps a customer journey across stages, touchpoints, emotional curve, pain points, and moments of truth into a markdown artifact with an optional mermaid timeline or flowchart. Use when synthesizing existing research into the shape of a customer's experience, end-to-end or for one phase. Without research signal yet, run discover-interview-synthesis or measure-survey-analysis first; refuses to fabricate emotional or behavioral data.

skills.name: discover-market-sizing
skills.description: Estimate market opportunity (TAM, SAM, SOM) using multiple sizing frameworks (top-down, bottom-up, comparable company, analogous market). Triangulates across frameworks, highlights where they converge and diverge as signal, and produces a calibrated range with source-graded confidence labels. Refuses unbounded fabrications; always offers a labeled lower-confidence path when data is thin. Used for investment cases, go/no-go decisions, and stakeholder pitches.

skills.name: discover-stakeholder-summary
skills.description: Maps the people and groups with a stake in a project, documenting their needs, concerns, influence, and engagement approach. Use at project kickoff, when taking over from another PM, or when resistance signals misalignment. For the update you send to those stakeholders, use foundation-stakeholder-update instead; this skill maps them, that one talks to them.

skills.name: foundation-build-risk-review
skills.description: Runs a fast pre-build risk review on a product idea, feature request, or scope change, naming the single assumption most likely to make it fail and returning a clear verdict (build small, validate first, pivot first, or don't build yet) with a no-code validation step. Use before committing build effort, when triaging whether to honor a feature request, or when deciding whether to expand scope, ahead of writing a PRD. For a launched product's pivot-or-persevere decision, use iterate-pivot-decision instead.

skills.name: foundation-lean-canvas
skills.description: Produces a one-page lean canvas across nine interlocking blocks (problem, customer, UVP, solution, channels, revenue, cost, metrics, unfair advantage) with optional inline HTML and SVG visual rendering. Use when framing a new product thesis, stress-testing an existing strategy, comparing strategic options side-by-side, or aligning a team on business-model assumptions. Works as a strategic hub that cross-links to deeper PM skills without duplicating them.

skills.name: foundation-meeting-agenda

skills.description: 법인등기소/인터넷등기소 상업등기 신청을 처음 하는 사용자를 위해 일반 영리 주식회사 발기설립 절차, 정관·첨부서류 실제 HWP 양식 작성, 등록면허세·과밀억제권역 중과 체크, rhwp 기반 순차 검토 흐름을 참고용으로 안내한다. 돌쇠에서는 가능한 가장 가까운 합법적 공식 단계까지 준비한다.

skills.name: layout-grid
skills.description: Define a responsive grid — columns, gutters, margins, and breakpoint behaviour. Use when establishing page structure. For the spacing scale inside components use `spacing-system`; for cross-device behaviour use `responsive-design`.

skills.name: color-system
skills.description: Build a product colour system — tonal scales, semantic roles, and contrast compliance. Use when defining or rebuilding colour from scratch. For dark-mode adaptation use `dark-mode-design`; for chart palettes use `data-visualization`; for multi-brand token architecture use `theming-system` (design-systems).

skills.name: handoff-spec
skills.description: Write the implementation handoff — measurements, behaviours, assets, states, and edge cases. Use when engineering picks up the work. For verifying the result afterwards use `design-qa-checklist`; for reusable library components use `component-spec` (design-systems).

skills.name: team-workflow
skills.description: Design the team's operating rhythm — task management, collaboration rituals, and tooling. Use when the day-to-day cadence needs structure. For a time-boxed sprint, use `design-sprint-plan`.

skills.name: law-of-closure
skills.description: Apply the Law of Closure — the eye completes implied shapes from partial forms. Use when reducing visual weight by dropping borders or letting negative space suggest structure. For explicit containers, use `law-of-common-region`.

skills.name: spacing-system
skills.description: Create a spacing scale from a base unit with rules for when each step applies. Use when standardising padding and margins. For page-level columns and gutters, use `layout-grid`.

skills.name: design-brief
skills.description: Write a project brief — problem space, constraints, audience, and success criteria. Use at kickoff for one specific project. For long-horizon aspiration use `north-star-vision`; for reusable decision rules use `design-principles`.

skills.name: design-critique
skills.description: Facilitate a structured team critique — framing, feedback rules, and actionable outcomes. Use when running a session with people in the room. For a solo expert review, use `heuristic-evaluation` (prototyping-testing).

skills.name: icon-system
skills.description: Specify an icon system — grid, sizing, stroke weight, naming, categories, and implementation. Use when standardising iconography. For broader illustration, use `illustration-style` (ui-design).

skills.name: dark-mode-design
skills.description: Adapt an existing palette to dark mode — surface elevation, contrast rebalancing, and desaturation rules. Use when you already have a light palette to translate. For building the base palette first, use `color-system`.

skills.name: law-of-proximity
skills.description: Apply the Law of Proximity — spatial closeness groups elements more strongly than any other cue. Use when spacing alone must carry grouping. For grouping via containers use `law-of-common-region`; via shared appearance use `law-of-similarity`.

skills.name: readable-measure
skills.description: Set line length and measure for comfortable reading across type sizes and breakpoints. Use when tuning body text. Covers measure only — for the full size and weight scale, use `typography-scale`.

skills.name: typography-scale
skills.description: Create a modular type scale with size, weight, and line-height relationships. Use when establishing typographic structure. For line length only use `readable-measure`; for judging type on an existing screen use `critique-typography` (visual-critique).

skills.name: visual-hierarchy
skills.description: Establish hierarchy through size, weight, colour, spacing, and position so the eye lands in the intended order. Use when composing new work. For judging an existing screen, use `critique-visual-hierarchy` (visual-critique).

skills.name: experience-map
skills.description: Map the full ecosystem of touchpoints, channels, and relationships across a service. Use when the experience spans more than one product. For one persona's linear journey use `journey-map` (design-research); for backstage operations use `service-blueprint`.

skills.name: empathy-map
skills.description: Build a Says, Thinks, Does, Feels map for one user or segment. Use when sharing user understanding quickly. For a composite archetype with goals and behaviours use `user-persona`; for cross-session themes use `affinity-diagram`.

skills.name: journey-map
skills.description: Map one persona's end-to-end experience with stages, touchpoints, emotions, and pain points. Use when improving an existing experience. For the multi-channel ecosystem use `experience-map` (ux-strategy); for screen-level paths use `user-flow-diagram` (prototyping-testing).

skills.name: design-token
skills.description: Define and organise tokens for colour, spacing, type, and elevation with naming and usage rules. Use when establishing the token layer. For auditing existing usage use `design-token-audit` (designer-toolkit); for multi-brand mapping use `theming-system`.

skills.name: case-study
skills.description: Craft a portfolio case study with narrative arc, process evidence, and outcomes. Use when telling a project's story to an external audience. For an internal stakeholder deck, use `presentation-deck`.

skills.name: ux-writing
skills.description: Write interface copy — microcopy, error messages, empty states, and CTAs. Use when the words are the deliverable. For content structure and ownership, use `content-strategy` (ux-strategy).

skills.name: law-of-continuity
skills.description: Apply the Law of Continuity — the eye follows alignment and unbroken paths. Use when sequencing steps, aligning content, or designing carousels and timelines. For grouping rather than sequencing, use `law-of-proximity`.

skills.name: law-of-similarity
skills.description: Apply the Law of Similarity — shared colour, shape, or size signals that elements belong to one category. Use when signalling relationships across distance. For grouping by position, use `law-of-proximity`.

skills.name: responsive-design
skills.description: Design layouts and interactions that adapt across screen sizes and input methods. Use when one design must serve many viewports. For the underlying column grid use `layout-grid`; for OS-specific patterns use `platform-conventions`.

skills.name: business-design
skills.description: Read financials, map competitive landscapes, and argue design decisions in the language of value. Use when defending design to commercial stakeholders. For the live negotiation itself, use `design-negotiation` (designer-toolkit).

skills.name: design-debt-audit
skills.description: Inventory and prioritise accumulated design inconsistencies across a product. Use when drift has built up over time. For token coverage specifically use `design-token-audit` (designer-toolkit); for WCAG gaps use `accessibility-audit` (design-systems).

skills.name: user-persona
skills.description: Build research-grounded personas with goals, frustrations, and behavioural patterns. Use when decisions need a consistent user reference. For one session's emotional snapshot use `empathy-map`; for motivation framing use `jobs-to-be-done`.

skills.name: motion-system
skills.description: Define motion tokens — durations, easing vocabulary, and reduced-motion handling — for consistency product-wide. Use when standardising motion across a system. For crafting one specific animation, use `animation-principles` (interaction-design).

skills.name: fitts-law
skills.description: Apply Fitts's Law — target acquisition time depends on size and distance. Use when sizing and positioning controls, especially for touch. For how many controls to show at once, use `hicks-law`.

skills.name: hicks-law
skills.description: Apply Hick's Law — decision time grows with the number of simultaneous choices. Use when a screen offers too many options at once. For how many items survive in memory afterwards, use `millers-law`.

skills.name: search-ux
skills.description: Design search — query input, zero results, refinement, and result presentation. Use when users retrieve rather than browse. For browse structure, use `navigation-patterns`.

skills.name: data-visualization
skills.description: Select chart types and design data encodings — marks, axes, labels, and accessible chart styling. Use when presenting data graphically. Owns chart selection and encoding only; the categorical colour ramp itself belongs to `color-system`.

skills.name: illustration-style
skills.description: Define an illustration style guide — visual language, colour usage, and application rules. Use when commissioning or standardising illustration. For icons, use `icon-system` (design-systems).

skills.name: content-strategy
skills.description: Define what content a product needs, how it is structured, and who owns it. Use when content itself is the problem. For the words in the interface use `ux-writing` (designer-toolkit); for structural hierarchy use `information-architecture`.

skills.name: design-sprint-plan
skills.description: Plan and facilitate a design sprint from challenge framing through prototype testing. Use when compressing discovery into days. For ongoing team cadence, use `team-workflow`.

skills.name: survey-design
skills.description: Design unbiased survey instruments — question wording, scales, and sampling — to measure attitudes at scale. Use when you need quantitative breadth. For behavioural experiments, use `a-b-test-design` (prototyping-testing).

skills.name: component-spec
skills.description: Specify one component — props, states, variants, accessibility, and usage rules. Use when defining a library component. For the reusable doc scaffold use `documentation-template`; for a problem-solution pattern use `pattern-library`.

skills.name: theming-system
skills.description: Design theming architecture — brand variants, dark mode, and high-contrast — mapped through token layers. Use when one system must serve multiple themes. For a single palette use `color-system` (ui-design); for dark mode craft use `dark-mode-design` (ui-design).

skills.name: jakobs-law
skills.description: Apply Jakob's Law — users expect your product to work like the others they already use. Use when deciding whether to innovate on a familiar pattern. For OS-mandated conventions specifically, use `platform-conventions` (ui-design).

skills.name: aesthetic-usability
skills.description: Apply the Aesthetic-Usability Effect — polished, consistent interfaces are perceived as more usable and forgive minor friction. Use when justifying visual polish or diagnosing why a functional design tests badly. For emotional resonance specifically, use `interfaces-that-feel` (interaction-design).

skills.name: von-restorff-effect
skills.description: Apply the Von Restorff Effect — the element that differs from its neighbours is the one remembered. Use when a single action must dominate. For overall ordering rather than single-element emphasis, use `visual-hierarchy`.

skills.name: design-principles
skills.description: Define actionable principles that resolve trade-offs when the team disagrees. Use when the same decisions keep getting relitigated. For a single project's framing, use `design-brief`.

skills.name: north-star-vision
skills.description: Articulate a long-horizon product vision that aligns teams and anchors strategy. Use when direction is contested or absent. For near-term project scope, use `design-brief`.

skills.name: service-blueprint
skills.description: Map service delivery across frontstage actions, backstage processes, and supporting systems. Use when staff and operations are part of the experience. For the customer-visible layer only, use `experience-map`.

skills.name: design-qa-checklist
skills.description: Build a QA checklist for verifying that a build matches the design. Use at implementation review. For the spec engineers build from, use `handoff-spec`.

skills.name: pattern-library
skills.description: Structure a pattern entry — problem context, solution, usage examples, and related patterns. Use when documenting a recurring solution rather than a component. For a single component's API, use `component-spec`.

skills.name: form-design
skills.description: Design a form end to end — field order, grouping, validation, and completion. Use when the artifact is a form. For product-wide error strategy use `error-handling-ux`; for first-run signup use `onboarding-design`.

skills.name: millers-law
skills.description: Apply Miller's Law — chunk information into groups of about four to fit working memory. Use when grouping fields, menu items, or steps. For reducing the number of choices offered, use `hicks-law`.

skills.name: teslers-law
skills.description: Apply Tesler's Law — every process has irreducible complexity that someone must absorb. Use when deciding whether the product or the user carries it. For reducing apparent choice, use `hicks-law`.

skills.name: law-of-common-region
skills.description: Apply the Law of Common Region — a shared container, background, or border groups elements regardless of spacing. Use when grouping must survive a tight layout. For grouping by spacing alone, use `law-of-proximity`.

skills.name: law-of-figure-ground
skills.description: Apply the Law of Figure-Ground — establish which layer is foreground and actionable versus background. Use when designing modals, overlays, and depth. For emphasising one element among peers, use `von-restorff-effect`.

skills.name: platform-conventions
skills.description: Design to iOS and Android conventions — what each OS mandates, where they diverge, and when to unify. Use when shipping native apps. For breakpoint adaptation use `responsive-design`; for matching competitor patterns use `jakobs-law` (interaction-design).

skills.name: metrics-definition
skills.description: Define UX metrics and KPIs that connect design decisions to measurable outcomes. Use when choosing what to measure. For presenting the results afterwards, use `design-impact-reporting` (design-ops).

skills.name: critique-color
skills.description: Critique a rendered screen's colour — contrast ratios, palette coherence, and semantic meaning. Use when reviewing one screen. For a product-wide WCAG audit use `accessibility-audit` (design-systems); for building the palette use `color-system` (ui-design).

skills.name: jobs-to-be-done
skills.description: Map functional, emotional, and social jobs with outcome expectations. Use when reframing decisions around motivation rather than features. For who the user is, use `user-persona`.

skills.name: design-review-process
skills.description: Establish review gates — criteria, checkpoints, and approval flow. Use when work ships without consistent review. For running one individual session, use `design-critique`.

skills.name: affinity-diagram
skills.description: Cluster many qualitative data points into themes and insight statements. Use when synthesising across multiple sessions or sources. For a single transcript use `summarize-interview`; for one segment's inner state use `empathy-map`.

skills.name: diary-study-plan
skills.description: Design a diary study — prompts, cadence, duration, participant criteria, and analysis frame. Use when behaviour unfolds over days or weeks. For a single-session study, use `usability-test-plan`.

skills.name: interview-script
skills.description: Write a structured interview guide — warm-up, core exploration, and wrap-up. Use before running interviews. For analysing what comes back, use `summarize-interview`.

skills.name: naming-convention
skills.description: Establish naming rules for components, tokens, and layers with patterns and worked examples. Use when names are inconsistent or being set. For what the tokens actually contain, use `design-token`.

skills.name: peak-end-rule
skills.description: Apply the Peak-End Rule — a flow is remembered by its most intense moment and its last. Use when designing completion, celebration, or cancellation moments. For sustaining engagement mid-flow, use `zeigarnik-effect`.

skills.name: state-machine
skills.description: Model component behaviour as explicit states, events, and transitions. Use when a component has many interacting states that must be exhaustive. For the feel and feedback of a single interaction, use `micro-interaction-spec`.

skills.name: competitive-analysis
skills.description: Compare UX patterns, features, strengths, and gaps across rival products. Use when you need to know what others actually do. For deliberately adopting their conventions, use `jakobs-law` (interaction-design).

skills.name: design-rationale
skills.description: Write rationale connecting decisions to user needs, business goals, and principles. Use when a decision needs defending in writing. For a live conversation, use `design-negotiation`.

skills.name: loading-states
skills.description: Design waiting experiences — spinners, skeletons, optimistic updates, and progressive reveal. Use when content takes time to arrive. For the latency budget itself use `doherty-threshold`; for success confirmation use `feedback-patterns`.

skills.name: test-scenario
skills.description: Write realistic usability task scenarios with success criteria and facilitation notes. Use when you have a study and need the tasks. For the surrounding study design, use `usability-test-plan` (design-research).

skills.name: opportunity-framework
skills.description: Identify, score, and prioritise design opportunities against impact and effort. Use when there are more ideas than capacity. For framing the one you choose, use `design-brief`.

skills.name: stakeholder-alignment
skills.description: Build alignment artifacts — responsibility matrices, decision rights, and communication plans. Use when unclear ownership stalls decisions. For persuading in the moment, use `design-negotiation` (designer-toolkit).

skills.name: design-impact-reporting
skills.description: Communicate design's contribution to business and user outcomes in stakeholder language. Use when reporting results upward. For choosing the metrics in the first place, use `metrics-definition` (ux-strategy).

skills.name: card-sort-analysis
skills.description: Analyse open or closed card sort results into a proposed grouping and label set. Use after running a sort study. For turning that evidence into a full structure, use `information-architecture` (ux-strategy).

skills.name: accessibility-audit
skills.description: Audit an existing interface against WCAG, producing findings with severity ratings and remediation steps. Use when you have a design or build to assess now. Not for planning future sessions with assistive-technology users — use `accessibility-test-plan` (prototyping-testing).

skills.name: localization-design
skills.description: Design for multiple languages, writing directions, and cultural contexts — text expansion, RTL mirroring, and locale formats. Use when shipping beyond one locale. For the words themselves, use `ux-writing` (designer-toolkit).

skills.name: presentation-deck
skills.description: Structure a design presentation for a specific audience and decision. Use when presenting internally. For a portfolio narrative use `case-study`; for the written argument use `design-rationale`.

skills.name: wireframe-spec
skills.description: Specify wireframe layout — content priority, component placement, and annotation. Use when defining structure before visual design. For grid mechanics, use `layout-grid` (ui-design).

skills.name: version-control-strategy
skills.description: Define version control for design files, components, and libraries — branching, naming, and release. Use when file history is chaotic. For design system contribution rules, use `design-system-governance` (design-systems).

skills.name: research-repository
skills.description: Build a repository that makes findings findable, reusable, and cumulative across teams. Use when the same research keeps getting redone. For synthesising one study, use `affinity-diagram`.

skills.name: summarize-interview
skills.description: Turn one interview transcript into themes, supporting quotes, and action items. Use immediately after a session. For synthesising many sessions at once, use `affinity-diagram`.

skills.name: usability-test-plan
skills.description: Design a usability study — research questions, methodology, participant criteria, metrics, and facilitation guide. Use when planning the study as a whole. For writing the task scenarios inside it, use `test-scenario` (prototyping-testing).

skills.name: design-negotiation
skills.description: Advocate for design quality, scope, and timeline with partners and leadership using evidence and shared goals. Use in the conversation itself. For the commercial vocabulary behind it, use `business-design` (ux-strategy).

skills.name: design-token-audit
skills.description: Audit token usage across a product for coverage, drift, and hard-coded values. Use when tokens exist and you suspect they are being bypassed. For defining tokens in the first place, use `design-token` (design-systems).

skills.name: gesture-patterns
skills.description: Design gesture interactions for touch and pointer — swipe, drag, long-press, and their discoverability. Use when input is gestural. For OS-standard gestures on iOS and Android, use `platform-conventions` (ui-design).

skills.name: zeigarnik-effect
skills.description: Apply the Zeigarnik Effect — incomplete tasks stay mentally active. Use when designing progress indicators, saved drafts, and return hooks. For the emotional shape of the ending, use `peak-end-rule`.

skills.name: a-b-test-design
skills.description: Design an A/B experiment — hypothesis, variants, primary metric, and sample size. Use when a change can be measured quantitatively at scale. For observing behaviour qualitatively, use `test-scenario`.

skills.name: click-test-plan
skills.description: Design first-click and click tests for findability and navigation. Use when testing whether people can locate something. For full task-based observation, use `test-scenario`.

skills.name: critique-affordance
skills.description: Critique a rendered screen's affordances — what looks clickable, state visibility, CTA clarity, and action discoverability. Use when reviewing an existing screen. For sizing and positioning targets in new work, use `fitts-law` (interaction-design).

skills.name: critique-typography
skills.description: Critique a rendered screen's typography — scale usage, readability, consistency, and token compliance. Use when reviewing type on a screen. For defining the scale itself, use `typography-scale` (ui-design).

skills.name: conversational-ux
skills.description: Design voice and conversational interfaces — dialog flows, error recovery, and persona. Use when the interface speaks and listens rather than being tapped. For graphical input collection, use `form-design`.

skills.name: doherty-threshold
skills.description: Apply the Doherty Threshold — keep system response under 400ms to preserve user flow. Use when diagnosing perceived slowness or setting a performance budget. For what to show during unavoidable waits, use `loading-states`.

skills.name: error-handling-ux
skills.description: Design error prevention, detection, and recovery across a product — message content, placement, and escape routes. Use when errors span multiple flows. For validation inside a single form, use `form-design`.

skills.name: feedback-patterns
skills.description: Design confirmations, status updates, and notifications that tell users an action registered. Use when the system must acknowledge success or change. For waiting states use `loading-states`; for failures use `error-handling-ux`.

skills.name: onboarding-design
skills.description: Design the first-run experience — activation path, progressive disclosure, and time to first value. Use for a user's very first session. For the mechanics of the signup form itself, use `form-design`.

skills.name: information-architecture
skills.description: Design content structure, hierarchy, labelling, and the navigation model. Use when organising what exists. For the UI that exposes it use `navigation-patterns` (interaction-design); for user-generated grouping evidence use `card-sort-analysis` (design-research).

skills.name: critique-composition
skills.description: Critique a rendered screen's composition — balance, whitespace, rhythm, and gestalt grouping. Use when a layout feels off but hierarchy is fine. For emphasis and eye flow specifically, use `critique-visual-hierarchy`.

skills.name: behavioural-analytics
skills.description: Read funnels, retention curves, and event data as a designer — separating a design problem from a tracking artefact. Use when handed product data you did not design and asked why people drop off. For choosing what to measure, use `metrics-definition` (ux-strategy); for running a controlled test, use `a-b-test-design` (prototyping-testing).

skills.name: documentation-template
skills.description: Generate a reusable documentation scaffold for components, patterns, or guidelines. Use when standardising how the system is documented. For the content of one component's spec, use `component-spec`.

skills.name: concept-selection
skills.description: Choose between competing concepts against criteria fixed in advance, and record what each rejected concept was testing. Use when several directions are alive and one has to win. For picking which problem to work on, use `opportunity-framework` (ux-strategy); for deciding by production traffic, use `a-b-test-design`.

skills.name: parallel-concepts
skills.description: Build several genuinely different solutions to the same problem at once, spread across what the user does rather than how it looks. Use when one direction is on the table and the team is about to refine it by default. For choosing between the concepts afterwards, use `concept-selection`.

skills.name: user-flow-diagram
skills.description: Diagram screen-level paths, decision points, and branch logic. Use when specifying how a feature is traversed. For the emotional end-to-end arc, use `journey-map` (design-research).

skills.name: navigation-patterns
skills.description: Select and design a navigation pattern — tabs, drawer, hierarchy, or hub — matched to product structure and user tasks. Use when choosing how users move between sections. For the underlying content structure, use `information-architecture` (ux-strategy).

skills.name: prototype-strategy
skills.description: Choose prototype fidelity and method to match the design question and the decision at stake. Use before building a prototype. For what to test once it exists, use `test-scenario`.

skills.name: design-system-governance
skills.description: Define how the system evolves — contribution model, versioning, deprecation, and change management. Use when multiple teams contribute. For driving uptake use `design-system-adoption` (designer-toolkit); for design file history use `version-control-strategy` (design-ops).

skills.name: design-system-adoption
skills.description: Create adoption strategy and enablement materials to drive design system usage. Use when the system exists but teams ignore it. For contribution and versioning rules, use `design-system-governance` (design-systems).

skills.name: animation-principles
skills.description: Apply animation principles — easing, staging, follow-through — to one specific UI motion. Use when tuning how an animation feels. For product-wide duration and easing tokens use `motion-system` (design-systems); for a full interaction spec use `micro-interaction-spec`.

skills.name: interfaces-that-feel
skills.description: Apply an emotional resonance lens to a UI that is technically correct but flat, prescribing changes at the copy, motion, and interaction layer. Use when a design tests fine but lands cold. For the polish-perception argument, use `aesthetic-usability` (ui-design).

skills.name: qual-quant-triangulation
skills.description: Reconcile what the numbers say with what users say, and design the study that settles it rather than restates it. Use when behavioural data and research findings point different ways. For reading the data on its own, use `behavioural-analytics`; for synthesising interviews on their own, use `affinity-diagram`.

skills.name: heuristic-evaluation
skills.description: Run an expert review against Nielsen's heuristics and domain criteria, with severity ratings. Use when you need findings without recruiting participants. For a facilitated team feedback session, use `design-critique` (design-ops).

skills.name: micro-interaction-spec
skills.description: Specify one micro-interaction completely — trigger, rules, feedback, loops, and modes. Use when handing a single interaction to engineering. For motion craft alone use `animation-principles`; for multi-state components use `state-machine`.

skills.name: serial-position-effect
skills.description: Apply the Serial Position Effect — first and last items in a sequence are recalled best. Use when ordering menus, lists, and steps. For emphasising one item regardless of its position, use `von-restorff-effect` (ui-design).

skills.name: critique-visual-hierarchy
skills.description: Critique a rendered screen's hierarchy — entry point, eye flow, weight distribution, and emphasis. Use when attention lands in the wrong place. For establishing hierarchy in new work, use `visual-hierarchy` (ui-design).

skills.name: critique-brand-consistency
skills.description: Critique a rendered screen against mood.md, voice.md, and tokens.md. Use when those brand files exist and you are checking compliance. For defining the visual language itself, use `illustration-style` (ui-design).

skills.name: accessibility-test-plan
skills.description: Plan accessibility testing — assistive technologies, participant criteria, WCAG coverage, and session protocol. Use when scheduling testing with real AT users. Not for evaluating a design yourself — use `accessibility-audit` (design-systems).

skills.name: critique-information-density
skills.description: Critique a rendered screen's density — cognitive load, content prioritisation, scanning patterns, and progressive disclosure. Use when a screen feels overwhelming. For the underlying choice-count principle, use `hicks-law` (interaction-design).

skills.name: docs-seo
skills.description: Runs on-page and technical SEO for a documentation site - indexability, canonicals and hreflang across versioned and translated pages, redirects, the generator's title and description templates, internal linking, and an owner-assigned fix list against an agreed pass threshold. Use whenever someone says "docs SEO", "our docs don't rank", "documentation search optimization", "the old version of our docs outranks the current one", "our docs pages aren't indexed", "fix the canonicals on our docs", "docs sitemap problems", "hreflang on our translated docs" or "preview docs got indexed" - even if th

skills.name: oss-launch

skills.description: Windows local privilege escalation playbook. Use when you have low-privilege shell access on Windows and need to escalate via token abuse, Potato exploits, service misconfigurations, DLL hijacking, UAC bypass, or registry autoruns.

skills.name: expression-language-injection
skills.description: Expression Language injection playbook. Use when Java EL, SpEL, OGNL, or MVEL expressions may evaluate attacker-controlled input in Spring, Struts2, Confluence, or similar frameworks.

skills.name: graphql-and-hidden-parameters
skills.description: GraphQL and hidden parameter testing playbook. Use when exploring introspection, batching, undocumented fields, hidden parameters, schema abuse, and GraphQL authorization gaps.

skills.name: business-logic-vulnerabilities
skills.description: Business logic vulnerability playbook. Use when reasoning about workflows, race conditions, price manipulation, coupon abuse, state machines, and multi-step authorization gaps.

skills.name: code-obfuscation-deobfuscation
skills.description: Code obfuscation analysis and deobfuscation playbook. Use when reversing binaries protected by junk code, opaque predicates, self-modifying code, control flow flattening, VM protection, or string encryption.

skills.name: smart-contract-vulnerabilities
skills.description: Smart contract vulnerability playbook. Use when auditing Solidity/EVM contracts for reentrancy, integer overflow, access control, delegatecall, flash loan, signature replay, and MEV-related attack patterns.

skills.name: authbypass-authentication-flaws
skills.description: Authentication bypass testing playbook. Use when assessing login flows, password reset logic, account recovery, MFA bypass, token predictability, brute-force resistance, and session boundary flaws.

skills.name: csrf-cross-site-request-forgery
skills.description: CSRF testing playbook. Use when reviewing state-changing web flows, anti-CSRF defenses, SameSite behavior, JSON CSRF, login CSRF, and OAuth state handling.

skills.name: insecure-source-code-management
skills.description: Source control and artifact exposure (.git, .svn, .hg, backups, .env). Use when recon finds VCS paths, 403 on hidden dirs, or backup/config leaks during authorized testing.

skills.name: idor-broken-object-authorization
skills.description: IDOR and broken object authorization testing playbook. Use when requests expose object identifiers, tenant boundaries, writable fields, or missing object-level authorization checks.

skills.name: ssrf-server-side-request-forgery
skills.description: SSRF playbook. Use when the server fetches URLs, resolves hostnames, imports remote content, or can be driven toward internal networks, cloud metadata, or secondary protocols.

skills.name: active-directory-kerberos-attacks
skills.description: Kerberos attack playbook for Active Directory. Use when targeting AD authentication via AS-REP roasting, Kerberoasting, golden/silver/diamond tickets, delegation abuse, or pass-the-ticket attacks.

skills.name: cors-cross-origin-misconfiguration
skills.description: CORS misconfiguration testing playbook. Use when analyzing cross-origin trust, credentialed browser reads, origin reflection, preflight policy bugs, and browser-based access to authenticated APIs.

skills.name: ssti-server-side-template-injection
skills.description: SSTI playbook. Use when template expressions, server-side rendering, preview features, or templating engines may evaluate attacker-controlled content.

skills.name: unauthorized-access-common-services
skills.description: Unauthorized access playbook for common exposed services. Use when Redis, Rsync, PHP-FPM, AJP/Ghostcat, Hadoop YARN, H2 Console, or similar management interfaces are exposed without authentication.
